newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Midday prices flat to firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Midday prices flat to firmer.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were even to slightly firmer at midday, as modest U.S. Treasury market gains helped tax-exempts regain composure after three straight losing sessions.

"We've been down in muni cash for the last three days in a row, and today it seems like the first day that prices are not going down," a municipal trader said. "They're even. They're probably going up a little bit if the government market catches much more of a bid here."

The 30-year Treasury bond was up 4/32 at 101-28/32 to yield 6.48 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 4/32 at 120-17/32. The September T-bond contract was up 5/32 at 114-24/32. The MOB spread was 185 ticks.
The bond market sold off Friday after economic data on employment and manufacturing showed strength. A trader, however, found some room for optimism within the downturn.
"It was not on a lot of volume, and you didn't see any follow-through selling yesterday or Monday," he said. "Since we haven't seen any selling, it seems now the pressure is off for the time being."
But the market still has to get through the U.S. Treasury's auction and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, which is set for release at 1400 EDT.

The government is scheduled to sell $12 billion of 10-year notes Wednesday during the second leg of its three-part quarterly refunding. The bidding deadline is 1300 EDT. On Thursday, $10 billion in 30-year bonds go on the block.

"I think the government market is not going to get too crazy...before the 30-year tomorrow, but I don't know," a trader said. "I mean the verdict is still out. I think we have a chance for prices to go higher, especially in the government area."

Munis are likely to face "tougher sledding," he said. Even though prices have cheapened since Friday, they are still not cheap enough for retail to care, the trader said. Retail investors don't want a 30-year bond that yields 5.40 percent to 5.45 percent, especially since they have to pay sales credits, which knocks the yield down to the low 5.0 percent to 5-1/4 percent range, he said.
Turning to new issues, EVEREN Securities Inc tentatively priced $101 million Rochester Community School District, Michigan, bonds at a top yield of 5.375 percent in 2017.
Also Wednesday, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter released the retail scale for a $464 million Allegheny County, Pa., airport revenue refunding bond deal. The top yield was set at 5.53 percent in 2016.
The retail order period runs until 1500 EDT Wednesday.
